A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AirZoo dataset, generation pipeline and three-task evaluation. Text, figures, tables and equations are readable and matchable across versions. The supplied v1 ends after its references; v2 additionally includes Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original geometric-consistency measurements and experiments on aerial retrieval, cross-view matching and reconstruction in Figure 4 and Tables 2–6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments in Figure 5 and Tables 3–7 and additionally reports scene-level results and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use the AirSim-Cesium-Unreal pipeline and fine-tune MegaLoc with weighted InfoNCE, RoMa with MegaDepth/AirZoo, and VGGT/DA3. The appendix newly documents trajectory design, controller operation and batching, without establishing a change to the underlying algorithms, architectures or objectives.

E1.justification: The three core tasks and named training/evaluation datasets remain. v2 adds a qualitative comparison of real DJI footage with synthetic renders at matching viewpoints and reports failures on building-orbit reconstruction sequences. Revised region/trajectory counts do not establish that particular geographic data were added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain the same methods: AnyLoc, SALAD, Game4Loc and MegaLoc for retrieval; LoFTR, ELoFTR, DUSt3R, MASt3R, RoMa and RoMa(GIM) for matching; and CUT3R, MapAnything, VGGT-SLAM, VGGT and DA3 for reconstruction. Supplementary comparisons reuse these baselines.

E3.justification: Reconstruction training changes from a reported 373 sequences to 361 trajectories, retaining 16 held-out trajectories. RoMa's AirZoo overlap range changes from 20–60% in v1 Section 4.2 to 30–50% in v2 Appendix C.1. These are reported setting revisions, without evidence that experiments were rerun. The added realism comparison uses matched viewpoints.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted analyses: real-versus-synthetic visual realism in Figure 6, a UAV-VisLoc Scene 7 error analysis supported by Table 8 and Figure 16, and a qualitative building-orbit failure report in Appendix D.4. These extend diagnostic coverage but do not constitute a systematic ablation or robustness suite.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed evaluations, confidence intervals or significance tests. The geometric-error CDF and median/P90/P95 reporting are retained. Additional scene-level scores do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: All numerical rows in v1 Tables 2–6 remain unchanged in v2 Tables 3–7. However, new Tables 8–10 substantially expand scene-level findings: Scene 7 retrieval R@1 falls from 38.46 for MegaLoc to 26.92 after fine-tuning, while City retrieval favors Game4Loc over the fine-tuned model, 21.12 versus 9.94. Some supplementary averages conflict with the main results: AnyLoc UAV-VisLoc R@1 is 2.57 in Table 8 versus 17.01 in Table 3. These are newly reported findings and inconsistencies, not demonstrated version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 newly gives formal definitions of footprint anchors, ray–ground-plane intersections and positive-tile membership; Appendix A.3 supplies the explicit pixel-to-global-coordinate transformation chain. This adds limited mathematical specification and geometric derivation. No theorem or proof is added; the standard F1 formula merely explains the retained metric.

C1.justification: The central geographic-diversity claim is materially redefined. v1 advertises 378 distinct regions and describes four weather trajectories per region; v2's abstract and introduction specify 95 base flight sequences producing 377 weather-conditioned trajectories. This changes what the advertised scale represents. The million-frame dataset, scalable simulator and three-task transfer contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific qualifications: Scene 7 degradation is attributed to unusual tile proportions and resizing distortion; building-orbit failures are attributed to missing surrounding-view training sequences; lighting/shading differences limit photometric realism; and unreliable IMU orientations motivate translation-only evaluation. These refine the retained generalization and domain-gap discussion.

D1.justification: Appendices A–D supply substantial missing reproducibility information: simulator control and coordinate handling, trajectory construction, retrieval batching/optimizer/epochs, RoMa mixture ratios, learning rates, resolution, training budget and hardware, and ground-truth construction. v2 also adds a project URL and explicitly documents geographic separation. Conversely, v1's statement of 1.1 million matching pairs from 55 regions is omitted. Most additions disclose existing procedures rather than establish experimental changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds a Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles reference, revises the critique of GIM toward limited long-term environmental variation, and changes MatrixCity's sequence-availability entry in Table 1 from available to unavailable. The broader literature coverage and research positioning remain.

P1.justification: v2 substantially expands explanatory structure through task-organized Appendices A–D, including simulator operation, loss motivation, sampling and annotation procedures. It rewrites the simulator explanation around component roles and the controller, adds Section 3.3 on dataset usage, and refines statistics terminology. The main section order remains, with additional front matter, corrected running headers and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: The visual presentation expands substantially with a simulator diagram, real/synthetic comparison, trajectory and annotation illustrations, additional qualitative comparisons, a train/test overview table and three scene-level result tables. Existing main figures and performance tables are largely retained and renumbered, while dataset-count labels and several captions are revised.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through Appendices A–D, clarifies geographic scale and exposes failures hidden by aggregate results. These are useful gains over v1's largely undocumented training and annotation procedures. However, the new supplementary results introduce unresolved inconsistencies: Table 8 reports AnyLoc and MegaLoc UAV-VisLoc R@1 averages of 2.57 and 25.72, versus 17.01 and 26.91 in Table 3. The added transparency supports a net improvement, but conflicting quantitative reporting limits its overall strength.
